source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I just thought of something.... I believe we should adjust the block prizes to
- Small = 1 x $500 every 100 sales.

The same net $ amount would still be given away, but this would create a smoother, cleaner, clearer, and more consistent flow of winners

process_items.label: Mint the ebook NFT
process_items.copy: Buy your ebook NFT for $15 USD. The mint number you receive becomes your referral code.

process_items.label: Earn Through Referrals
process_items.copy: Share either your mint number or your link. Whenever someone mints with it, you immediately earn $5 USD. There are no limits and no expiration. If no code is provided → the $5 + tickets are awarded to a random existing ticket holder.

process_items.label: Build Up Tickets
process_items.copy: Every referral also awards you Small & Big Block prize tickets for the current blocks. More referrals = more tickets = greater chances.

process_items.label: Enter the Prize Draws
process_items.copy: Small Block: 1 × $500 awarded every 100 sales. Big Block: 1 × $10,000 awarded every 10,000 sales. (Sales = mint + secondary) Chainlink VRF selects the winners randomly and fairly.

process_items.label: Receive Your Rewards
process_items.copy: Commissions are delivered automatically on-chain. Prize wins are posted on the Winners page and can be claimed with one click whenever you're ready.

decisions.reason: A complete same-message MODIFY already records one $500 winner every 100 sales and removes the prior approximate-interval interpretation.
The source changes prize batching parameters while explicitly preserving the net giveaway amount; it does not change mint price, founder share, referral commission, or active pool destinations.
Changing winner counts and draw intervals does not alter Chainlink VRF, ticket weighting, eligible holders, on-chain execution, or verification.
The prize-parameter change does not alter which NFT-associated entitlements, badges, referral identity, or active and expired ticket states transfer on resale.
The Mission page explicitly states the superseded Small and Big Block winner counts and sales intervals, so its prize-pool copy necessarily changes.

approved_sections.heading: Our Purpose
approved_sections.content: Project Rebuild is presented as a movement to repair publishing through a fair and transparent FAMM ecosystem that rewards creators and fans without gatekeepers or artificial hype.

approved_sections.heading: Community First
approved_sections.content: Each community member's success contributes to collective growth and shared momentum.

approved_sections.heading: Fair Rewards
approved_sections.content: Rewards are unlimited, transparent, on-chain, and provided without hidden terms or middlemen.

approved_sections.heading: Innovation
approved_sections.content: The project uses NFTs, smart contracts, and decentralized technology, beginning by proving FAMM and aiming to become a full DAO after momentum builds.

approved_sections.heading: Long-Term Vision
approved_sections.content: The project aims to create sustainable, lasting value and scale from one underdog story into a platform for everyone.

approved_sections.heading: What We're Building
approved_sections.content: Describe referral rewards; Small Block prizes of 1 × $500 every 100 sales and Big Block prizes of 1 × $10,000 every 10,000 sales using Chainlink VRF; badges and leaderboards; on-chain transparency; and automated payouts.

approved_sections.heading: Join the Movement
approved_sections.content: Invite users to join a community where their contributions are valued and their success is rewarded.

decisions.reason: The source does not change the mint-number referral identity, its permanence, sharing methods, display surfaces, or resale behavior.
The source changes prize draw parameters but does not change the $5 no-referral commission or its random-holder allocation.
Both Small and Big Block mechanisms remain active, so both ticket counters and the existing permanent badges and referral-code metadata remain valid unchanged.
The prize-parameter adjustment has no effect on the current or planned product names.
Counting secondary sales toward prize draws does not change the enabled flat $10 secondary-sale royalty.
